lessons.title: A school club announcement
objectives: Understand the main purpose of a short school announcement.
Identify simple details such as day, room, time and things to bring.
Follow a simple instruction for new club members.

explanation.en: Listen once to understand the situation. Listen again for simple details such as the day, room number, start time and what students should bring. Do not use the transcript before answering.
explanation.vi: Nghe lần đầu để hiểu tình huống chung. Nghe lại để tìm các chi tiết đơn giản như ngày, phòng, giờ bắt đầu và đồ cần mang theo. Không xem transcript trước khi trả lời.

audio_asset.source_text: Teacher: Hello, students. Here is a message about the photography club. The club meets this Thursday in Room 12. The meeting starts at four o'clock and finishes at five. Please bring a pencil and your phone or camera if you have one. You do not need to bring money. The club will provide paper and photo cards. New students should arrive ten minutes early to write their names on the club list. If you cannot come this week, the next meeting is on Thursday the fourteenth.
audio_asset.fallback: If playback is unavailable, mark listening unassessed; do not reveal the transcript first or award listening credit.

lessons.title: A changed plan for Saturday
objectives: Understand the purpose of a short conversation about a changed plan.
Identify revised times, meeting points and things to bring.
Make simple inferences from reasons and conditions in the conversation.

explanation.en: When a plan changes, listen for contrast between the old plan and the new one. Separate the meeting time from the departure time, and notice reasons such as because or so. Listen twice before answering if needed.
explanation.vi: Khi kế hoạch thay đổi, hãy phân biệt thông tin cũ và mới. Tách giờ gặp khỏi giờ khởi hành, và chú ý lý do với các từ như because hoặc so.

audio_asset.source_text: Emma: Hi Ben. I'm calling about our science museum trip on Saturday. The bus was going to leave school at nine, but the driver has changed the time. It will leave at nine thirty now, so please meet at the school gate at nine fifteen. Ben: Okay. Do we still need to bring lunch? Emma: Yes. The museum café is closed for repairs, so bring a packed lunch. The school will provide water. Ben: Do we need money for the ticket? Emma: No, the teacher has already paid for the tickets. You only need money if you want to buy something in the gift shop. Ben: What time will we get back? Emma: Around three forty-five. Also, if your plans change and you cannot come, tell Ms Brown by Friday at twelve.

lessons.title: Discussing a group-project problem
objectives: Identify the main problem and proposed solution in a planning conversation.
Understand details about deadlines, roles and constraints.
Infer why speakers prefer one solution or explanation over another.

explanation.en: At B1, listen for the problem, the options speakers consider and the reason they finally prefer one option. Contrast words and practical constraints often reveal attitude and intention. Exact details such as deadlines still matter.
explanation.vi: Ở mức B1, hãy nghe để xác định vấn đề, các phương án được cân nhắc và lý do người nói chọn một phương án. Các từ chỉ tương phản và hạn chế thực tế thường thể hiện thái độ hoặc ý định.

audio_asset.source_text: Maya: We need to finish our presentation by Friday. The slides are almost done, but the survey chart is hard to read because I tried to show all sixty responses at once. Leo: Why don't we group similar responses into three categories? We can keep the full data in our notes in case the teacher asks about it. Maya: Good idea. I was also going to print colour copies for everyone, but that will be expensive. Leo: Let's make one large poster and share the full file online. The school printer can produce an A3 poster for free, but we have to send the file before four o'clock on Wednesday. Maya: Then I'll revise the chart tonight and send you a draft on Tuesday. Could you check it before lunch on Wednesday? Leo: Yes. I have football after school, so morning is better for me. Maya: One more thing. Twelve students skipped one survey question, and I'm worried people will think our data is incomplete. Leo: Add a note explaining that the question was optional. That makes the missing answers clear. Maya: Right. And during the presentation, let's focus on two main findings instead of reading every number.

lessons.title: Build a clear opinion paragraph
objectives: Analyse an opinion prompt and choose relevant ideas.
Organise an opinion, reason, example and conclusion into a coherent paragraph.
Use suitable linkers, register and language choices before drafting a longer response.

explanation.en: Before writing, identify the exact question and decide your position. Build one clear line of support: opinion → reason → specific example → concluding link. Cohesive words such as because, for example, however and therefore should show a real relationship between ideas, not simply decorate the paragraph. Clear, relevant language is more important than unnecessarily difficult vocabulary.
explanation.vi: Trước khi viết, hãy xác định đúng yêu cầu đề và chọn quan điểm. Xây dựng một mạch rõ ràng: ý kiến → lý do → ví dụ cụ thể → câu kết. Từ nối phải thể hiện quan hệ thật giữa các ý, không chỉ được thêm vào cho có.

examples: OPINION · I think schools should give students one homework-free evening each week.
REASON · This can help students recover and manage other responsibilities.
EXAMPLE · For example, they could use that evening for sport, family time or reading.
CONCLUSION · Therefore, one planned break can support a healthier weekly routine.

activities.prompt: Prompt: 'Should schools give students one homework-free evening each week?' What must the writer do?

options.text: Give an opinion and support it
Write only a list of homework tasks
Explain how to become a teacher

feedback.explanation_en: The task asks for a position on the idea and support for that position.

activities.prompt: Which opening states a clear opinion?

options.text: I think one homework-free evening each week can be useful for students.
Homework is a word with eight letters.
There are many days in a week.

feedback.explanation_en: The first sentence gives a direct position on the question.

activities.prompt: Which reason most directly supports the opinion that one free evening can help students?

options.text: It can give students time to recover and manage other responsibilities.

feedback.explanation_en: The first reason is directly relevant to the proposed homework-free evening.

activities.prompt: Which example best develops the reason in Q3?

options.text: For example, a student could use that evening for sport, family time or reading.
For example, homework has many pages.
For example, Tuesday comes after Monday.

feedback.explanation_en: The example gives concrete ways a free evening could support recovery and balance.

activities.prompt: Choose the best linker: 'A free evening may help students rest. ___, it should not mean that important work is ignored.'

feedback.explanation_en: However correctly introduces a contrast or limitation.

activities.prompt: Choose the best linker: 'Students often have schoolwork, clubs and family responsibilities. ___, one planned break can make the week easier to manage.'

feedback.explanation_en: Therefore introduces a result or conclusion from the previous idea.

activities.prompt: Which order makes the clearest paragraph plan?

options.text: Reason → new topic → opinion → different topic

feedback.explanation_en: A clear B1 opinion paragraph can follow opinion, reason, example and conclusion.

activities.prompt: Which sentence has the most suitable neutral school-writing register?

options.text: Students may benefit from having one evening without assigned homework.
Kids totally need a night with zero annoying stuff.
Homework is, like, super bad sometimes.

feedback.explanation_en: The first sentence is clear, neutral and appropriate for a school opinion paragraph.

activities.prompt: Which sentence is grammatically correct and clear?

options.text: One planned break can help students manage their time more effectively.
One planned break can helps students manages their time.
One planned break helping students to managed their time.
One planned break can helped students manage time more effective.

feedback.explanation_en: Can is followed by the base verb help, and effectively is the correct adverb form.

activities.prompt: Should schools give students one homework-free evening each week? Give your opinion, at least one clear reason and one specific example. Write about 120–160 words.
